blocks.closing.title:
The Room
You Are Received In.
blocks.closing.body:
A diwan is not a dining room. It is the long low room a
          household keeps for receiving people in — cushions down both walls, coffee
          arriving whether you asked or not, and nobody counting how long you stay. Half
          the name over this door is that word, which is a promise about the room rather
          than about the food, and it is the harder of the two to keep.
blocks.about.opening: One room, on Haile Selassie Road, next to the Ola station. The carte
blocks.about.carte: runs to a hundred and sixty-six things across nineteen courses —
blocks.locale.body:
One room, downtown, on Haile Selassie Road next to the Ola
      station. Google rates it 4.7 across three hundred and twenty-three reviews, and
      reports that people spend anywhere from twenty-five minutes to three hours here
      — which is a wide spread for a place that calls itself a fast food and
      cafe.
blocks.faq.where.a: One room, downtown. Haile Selassie Road, next to the Ola petrol station, in the United Meat Supplies building, Mombasa 80100.
blocks.index.caption:
The doors open at noon and the grill is already lit, because the rice
            has been on since long before that. Nineteen courses run from then
            until eleven at night. Eleven hours, one kitchen, one room.
blocks.index.beyond: Mandi under a lid, a burger, eighteen coffees and five kinds of kunafa. A hundred and sixty-six things across nineteen courses — which is what it takes to be the grill and the cafe at the same time.
blocks.menu.carteNote:
Everything here is on from noon until eleven, seven days a week. Nineteen
          courses and a hundred and sixty-six dishes, and not one alcoholic drink
          among them — the thirteen mojitos are mocktails, and so is everything
          on the juice board.
blocks.about.stmt:
a charcoal grill, rice cooked under a lid, a sandwich counter, eighteen
            coffees and five kinds of kunafa. What it is not is a restaurant that
blocks.about.ch1.lede: Nothing on the main course is cooked in a pan. Mishkaki, kofta, shish tauk, chicken pousin, a T-bone, a whole half chicken — all of it goes over heat, which is the one method that leaves a cook nowhere to hide. Fourteen dishes on that board and every one of them is finished by the same fire.
blocks.about.ch1.n1:
<dt>Fourteen off the grill</dt>
                <dd>From chicken wings at 600 shillings to the full mixed platter at 2,500, which is the most expensive thing the kitchen sells.</dd>
blocks.about.ch2.lede: Mandi, hanith, zurbian, madhabi. Four Yemeni and Gulf rice dishes, where the meat goes in above the rice and everything that comes off it during the hours it cooks goes into the grain below. It is the slowest thing this kitchen does and the one that has to be started before the doors open.
blocks.about.ch2.n1:
<dt>Nine rice dishes</dt>
                <dd>Three in mutton at 800 shillings, six in chicken — breast or legs, at 800 and 780. The price difference is the cut, not the cooking.</dd>
blocks.about.ch2.n2: <dd>Mandi is the pot it steams in, hanith the way it is hung, zurbian the spicing and madhabi the finish over coals. Four names, one cut of meat.</dd>
blocks.about.ch3.head: Five Kinds of Kunafa
blocks.about.ch3.lede: Plain, chocolate, lotus, caramel, pistachio. Most kitchens that serve kunafa serve one; this one keeps five on the board, next to maasoub and arika in half and full, basbousa plain and toffee, and a waffle. Shredded pastry over hot cheese is not a thing you can hold back and reheat.
blocks.about.ch3.n1:
<dt>Thirteen on the board</dt>
                <dd>Five kunafas, maasoub and arika in two sizes each, two basbousas, a waffle and a plate of mini pancakes.</dd>
blocks.about.ch3.n2:
<dt>200 to 800 shillings</dt>
                <dd>From a basbousa to the pistachio kunafa. Cheaper than the grill and, going by what people photograph, the reason a good many of them came.</dd>
blocks.about.ex1: Mishkaki, kofta, shish tauk, a T-bone and a whole chicken, cooked over heat rather than in a pan. Fourteen dishes on one board is not a section — it is what the kitchen is built around.
blocks.about.ex3: Thirteen of them, from a 200-shilling basbousa to the pistachio kunafa. It is open as long as the kitchen is, which is why the room is still full at eleven at night.
blocks.faq.alcohol.a: No. There is not one alcoholic drink among the hundred and sixty-six things on this carte. The thirteen mojitos are mocktails — lemon, passion, blue lagoon, green mountain and the rest — and so is everything on the juice board, including the one called a Cocktail Juice. What there is instead is a coffee bar: eighteen hot, nine frappuccinos, six iced, and thirteen milkshakes beside them.
blocks.faq.halal.rest:
kitchen is Middle Eastern, and there is no pork on any of the nineteen
            courses — but that is an observation about a menu, not a statement from
blocks.faq.cuisine.a: Middle Eastern, and more precisely than that phrase usually means. Yemeni and Gulf rice cooked under a lid — mandi, hanith, zurbian, madhabi. Levantine mezze and grills — hummus, mutabal, fatoush, shish tauk, kofta. Egyptian plates — fuul, shakshuka, kebda, adas. Mishkaki, which is the coast's own. And beside all of it, pizza, burgers, pasta and a full coffee bar, because the sign over the door says fast food and cafe as well.
blocks.faq.veg.a: A good many, and they are countable off the carte: falafel three ways, fuul, adas, fasuolia, hummus, mutabal, labanies taboula, cucumber yoghurt, four salads, the vegetable pizza, grilled vegetables, mashed potatoes and five kinds of chips. Vegan and gluten-free are not confirmed for this

blocks.dish.title: Mix Grilled Platter
blocks.dish.n1: Minced, spiced and pressed onto the skewer by hand, so it cooks in the shape of the hand that made it. On the carte on its own as well, as a plate, which is how you find out how much of the platter is this.
blocks.dish.n2: Chicken, marinated and then grilled fast so the outside takes colour before the inside has time to dry. The kitchen sells it three ways — as a plate, in a sandwich, and here.
blocks.dish.n3: The coast's own skewer, and the one item on this platter that belongs to Mombasa rather than to the Gulf. A platter is a dish you are meant to use your hands on, and this is the part that proves it.
blocks.dish.n4: Every meal is served with side of your choice — the menu's own line, on its own board. Seven of them, from plain chips to the house chips, which is the thing most people here order first.
blocks.about.ch2.label: Chapter II — The rice
blocks.about.ch2.head: Cooked Under the Lid
blocks.about.ch4.dd: <dd>Noon until eleven at night. Google reports people typically spend anywhere from twenty-five minutes to three hours here, which is a wide spread for one room.</dd>
blocks.about.exCoffee: Eighteen hot coffees, nine frappuccinos and six iced, from a 150-shilling espresso to a hazelnut latte. A grill that also runs a proper coffee bar is doing two jobs, and this one prices both.
